artifact: CLOSE — G-97 R2, render Police and Fire and EMS
status: OPEN FOR MERGE — planner-owned. Not merged, not deployed.
missionPremise: Eleven domains have generated deterministic fixture data since G-91 and G-92 and reached NO pixel; four consecutive waves built everything underneath the lenses and never the lenses (OPS-17 A-081, which records the deferral as the planner's). The seam already distinguishes four source states, and until a lens rendered one, a customer could not tell 'we did not build this' from 'your city has no source for this' — which is ruling 1 and the reason patrol-vehicles is kept gated on an ungranted vendor. This lane's job was to make that difference visible on the two lenses that carry the only deliberately ungranted region in the product.
completionPredicate: A stranger opens /?lens=police and /?lens=fire-ems on template-city and reads records with their counting rules and provenance; reads the Patrol roster stating it is BUILT and sourceless with Spireon and the pack named; opens the same URLs with cityKey=empty-city and finds every region reachable, quiet, and carrying its own basis; and can tell ungranted from granted-empty by reading the screen alone. CI check-run conclusion strings are 'success'. axe on the lane's surfaces is clean of conformance rules in BOTH themes with no node added. All four are met and each is evidenced below with raw output.
scopeBasis: The dispatch scoped this lane to <section id="lens-police">, <section id="lens-fire-ems"> and the CSS added for them, because three rendering lanes were building into one web/index.html and one web/shell.css and the planner merges serially. The final diff is THREE files — those two sections, an appended block in web/app.js, and one new test file — and touches no shared test, no stylesheet, no server route and no nav markup. That is narrower than the lane's first commit, deliberately: R3 merged mid-flight with a renderer that does the same job, so this lane deleted its own and composed R3's. Out of scope and untouched: R1's development-services section, R3's fleet and public-works sections, web/sc-kit.css, every feed and grant, G-24, L26, live Bastrop.

findings.severity: product defect, found and fixed, then superseded by the convergence
findings.what: the lane's first renderer read its three regions IN SERIES, so the last region on a lens painted three round trips late. On Police the late one is the Patrol roster — the region this row exists to make visible — and it sat reading 'Not read' beside a fully populated Camera inventory: a failure state dressed as a loading state.
findings.howFound: the rendered walk read the roster as unrendered; the diagnosis was the loop order, not the markup
findings.disposition: fixed by reading concurrently, then carried forward by the convergence, where loadPoliceLens issues both reads through Promise.all

findings.severity: instrument defect in this lane's own walk, fixed twice
findings.what: the walk waited on the FIRST region's caption only, so it read the DOM before the rest of the lens had painted and would have certified a green surface with an unrendered roster. After the convergence the same instrument broke the other way: R3's renderer leaves the caption reading 'Not read' for EVERY non-ok state, so a caption-based signal can never be satisfied on an ungranted or empty region — which is most of what this walk exists to read.
findings.fix: wait on the KICKER, for every region on the lens
findings.why it matters: twice in one lane an instrument stopped measuring before the thing it measures had happened. It is the same shape as R2-F1 one layer up.

findings.severity: environment, measured and worked around, NOT a product change
findings.what: web/index.html loads a render-blocking Google Fonts stylesheet, and a type=module script cannot execute until it resolves. On this machine that link was taking tens of seconds, which timed out three consecutive walks and one full axe pass, and looked exactly like a product hang. The first two diagnoses were both wrong.
findings.measured: with the third-party stylesheet answered by an empty 200, commit-to-navigation is 29 to 91 ms; without it, page.goto exceeded 30 s. A networkidle axe pass returned 'scanned 0/4' — a VACUOUS pass, reported as such rather than as clean.
findings.carriedForward: every instrument in this lane intercepts THIRD-PARTY ONLY by URL predicate and answers stylesheets with an empty 200. A catch-all route that merely continues local requests STALLS them, which produced two further false negatives before it was measured. Both arms of every before/after pair run through the identical interception.

findings.severity: gate interaction, four instances, each fixed in this lane
findings.what: four product gates fired on this lane's own PROSE rather than on its behaviour: `typeof kind.id === "string"` read as an element-id comparison to the addressability gate and demanded an id named 'string'; the characters 'rgb(' inside a CSS comment tripped the no-colour-function rule; a comment quoting the three forbidden freshness strings tripped the freshness rule; and this lane's own CSS assertion went red on the words 'no font-size' inside its own comment.
findings.reading: all four are DEV_PROCESS 2.6 — a source file parsed by a tool has a character set, and these gates read comments. Every one is a gate working. Recorded because the next rendering lane will hit at least one.

findings.severity: PRODUCT-LINE FINDING, routed to the planner, not fixed here
findings.what: the kit pair --sc-ok #2F7A52 on --sc-ok-wash #E3F0E8 measures 4.444:1 in the LIGHT theme against the 4.5:1 AA threshold for normal text at 12px/500. It is 0.056 short.
findings.measuredIndependently: computed in-page from the two computed colours on both arms, and reproduced by axe. This lane measured it before reading R3's reasoning; R3 reports the same pair at 4.44:1, which is two independent measurements agreeing.
findings.preExisting: YES, and proven rather than assumed. On main, the Development services lens renders two ready-to-issue pills through p-ok at exactly that computed pair and axe flags both at viewport 1440x1200.
findings.minimumFix: #2E7750 measures 4.623:1 on the wash, 5.425:1 on --sc-surface and 5.096:1 on --sc-surface-2. The dark arm needs nothing: #55BE86 on the dark surface measures 7.679:1.
findings.whyNotFixedHere: web/sc-kit.css is byte-identical across smartcity-dashboards, smart-files and plan-review, its own header says a repo that edits a token value has forked the system, and this dispatch names the file untouchable. G-94 raised --sc-ink-3 and --sc-quiet without reaching --sc-ok, so this is the same class of finding that row was opened for.
findings.howThisLaneAvoidedIt: by adopting R3's merged rule that a RESOLVED status renders quiet, which is the visual law rather than a workaround — twelve online cameras and eight in-service trucks are the rows that need nobody, and eight coloured pills are the loudest thing on the page. Development services still renders ready-to-issue through p-ok, so ONE severity vocabulary now has TWO renderings across the product line. That divergence is named here as a product-line call and is NOT settled by this lane.

findings.severity: INSTRUMENT FINDING, material to the VPAT/ACR work
findings.what: axe's color-contrast rule evaluates only what is inside the VIEWPORT. Every contrast baseline on this product is therefore a function of viewport height, and the G-95 gate and baseline run at 1440x900.
findings.divergenceTest: main's Development services lens has two failing p-ok pills; at 1440x900 both are below the fold and axe reports 0 nodes, at 1440x1200 both are in view and axe reports 2. On an earlier build of this branch the Police lens reported 5 of 12 at 900 and 12 of 12 at 2400. In EVERY arm axe's node count equalled the count of failing elements whose bounding box intersected the viewport, exactly.
findings.consequence: a surface scored clean at 1440x900 is clean ABOVE THE FOLD, which is a different claim from clean. Content inside a scrolling column is systematically undercounted, and this product puts its record tables inside .colstack, which scrolls.
findings.routedTo: G-95 / the wave-3 manual protocol and the ACR scope map. Not fixed here; this lane owns no scanner in the repo.

findings.severity: GATE ENVIRONMENT FINDING, reported because it nearly produced a wrong verdict
findings.what: the G-95 a11y gate FAILED on this branch when run locally on Windows with 44 unresolved color-contrast nodes on #nav-demonstrated and #nav-sources-rule, reason elmPartiallyObscuring, against an adjudicated ceiling of 1 — reproduced twice, real exit code 1. The same commit's a11y check-run on the Linux CI runner concluded 'success'.
findings.reading: G-95's own REVIEW_ITEMS entry records this finding as environment-dependent and measured it in the OPPOSITE direction (2 nodes on a Linux runner, 0 on the author's Windows machine). This lane is a third measurement and it disagrees with both: 44 on Windows, 0 on Linux. The cause the entry names is real — .nav-foot is position:sticky with an opaque background over a scrolling nav list, and axe will not composite a background through a sticky overlap — and the lane's runtime nav badges make the list about 20 px taller with real fonts, which is enough to move the count.
findings.whatWasNOTDone: no attempt to make the local gate green. The entry's own remedy ('when .nav-foot stops overlapping the nav list, or when the footer's figures move somewhere that does not need a sticky bar') is declared a UI decision that is not a lane's to take, and this lane agrees. The authoritative number is the CI check-run conclusion, which is 'success'.
findings.carriedForward: an adjudication whose node count varies from 0 to 44 across two operating systems is a ceiling nobody can set correctly. That is a control-design question for whoever owns the gate.

findings.what: a local server PID file was overwritten by a later start, orphaning the first process; port 8113 was still answering after both recorded PIDs had been killed and verified dead. Found by probing the PORT rather than trusting the kill, and cleared by resolving the listener's owning process.
findings.reading: a kill verified against a remembered pid is not a kill verified against the resource. Probe what you actually care about.

findings.what: R3's renderRegion writes the region caption as 'Not read' for every non-ok state, including ungranted and granted-empty. The region HAS been read; what it lacks is a source. The kicker, head and basis all carry the true state, so nothing on the surface is wrong, but the caption is the one string that says less than it knows.
findings.disposition: not changed. It is shared merged code, four lenses read it, and changing one string there is a product-line wording call rather than this lane's.

theConvergence.whatHappened: This lane's first commit shipped its own four-state resolver in a NEW served module src/domain-render.mjs, imported by web/app.js at /domain-render.mjs and imported directly by the Node suite, so that granted-empty could be proven behaviourally in the bare-Node run. While that was in flight, G-97 R3 merged the same rule inline in web/app.js.
theConvergence.theCall: DELETE this lane's resolver and compose R3's. Two implementations of one rule on one page is the CTRL-1 shape this program has paid for twice, and a merged implementation beats an unmerged one. renderRegion, renderRegionMetrics, statusLabelsFor, loadDomain, unreadRegion, applyLensState, sourcedLabel and sourcedRule are all reused; src/public-safety-lenses.test.mjs asserts each is declared EXACTLY ONCE in the served script, so a third copy fails by name.
theConvergence.whatItCost: the four-state copy is no longer exercised by a Node test against a seam-composed payload; it is asserted textually in R3's src/render-lenses.test.mjs and behaviourally in this lane's rendered walk. Stated rather than hidden.
theConvergence.whatItBought: one sentence per state across four lenses; three files changed instead of eight; no shared test moved, so nothing in R1's path was disturbed; no server route added; and no CSS at all.
theConvergence.alsoReverted: the ownership stretch declared at CP1. This lane had changed the static nav badge for both lenses from 'Not built' to 'Empty' and moved the src/ui.test.mjs assertion that pins it. R3 had already settled the question the other way — leave the static badge as the pre-read fallback and write the live one through applyLensState at runtime — so the markup and the shared test were both restored to the merged precedent.
